idiom_name: RSpec/Minitest with committed fixture files, or the approvals gem for the off-the-shelf loop
implementation_notes: RSpec and Minitest provide runners and matchers, not a snapshot store, so a characterization test is hand-written: capture the subject's output, read the committed reference from spec/fixtures/, compare with the eq matcher and allow rewriting only behind an explicit environment variable (review the resulting diff before committing). The approvals gem supplies the same loop as a library - its README describes it as a library for golden-master style testing in Ruby, with approved/received files and an approve step - so choose it when a dependency is acceptable and the ceremony should be standardized. The hand-written form remains the norm in RSpec suites that already keep fixtures, and Ruby's duck typing makes it easy to render only the observable projection of the subject.
code_sketch:
RSpec.describe LegacyPricing do
  it "pins the current quote output" do
    got = described_class.quote("A-1", 2)
    golden = "spec/fixtures/golden/quote_A-1.txt"
    File.write(golden, got) if ENV["UPDATE_GOLDEN"]  # review the diff, then commit
    expect(got).to eq(File.read(golden))
  end
end
pitfalls: Object#inspect and to_yaml of arbitrary Ruby objects embed object ids and implementation details; serialize an explicit projection instead of dumping the object.
The update branch is a two-line footgun: if UPDATE_GOLDEN is set in a pipeline the suite rewrites its own references, so assert the flag is absent on CI.
Reading references relative to the current working directory breaks when a single spec file is run from a different directory; resolve paths from __dir__ or the spec root.
